caption.text: One page answers whether anything needs you this week. When the answer is no, it says so and leaves it there.

scenes.why: How Home Base helps with this moment, in the listing's own words, on the real screen that shows it. Screen: "A couple of things need a look" (Your home now: what's wrong, what to care for, what's coming up and what's handled, with the fridge and a dripping tap flagged.) chosen because it is the real screen closest to "One page answers whether anything needs you this week. When the answer is no, it"; focus on "Wrong, To care for, Coming up, Handled".
Ends on where to read the whole guide, with the product beneath it: the viewer leaves with the next step, not only a pitch.

reasoning.decision: Facebook feed video, 1080×1350, 10–30s, hook by 1.5s, sound off
reasoning.because: Scrolled past in a feed with sound off: say who it is for in the first seconds, name the product early, keep every point on screen and readable at a glance.

reasoning.decision: Home Base: $49 (list $99), motif "tag", calm personality, cool accent #4f7a5c
reasoning.because: From its definition and Shop listing. 3 real screens to show.

One real moment from Home Base's listing (searchedProblems[5].phrase). The film is about this moment and how the product helps with it: "One page answers whether anything needs you this week. When the answer is no, it says so and leaves it there."

reasoning.decision: "How to make a home binder you can safely share" (draftpace.com/guides/how-to-make-a-home-binder)
reasoning.because: The guide that covers this moment: what to do comes from it, and the film ends on it.

reasoning.decision: Before launch: helpful and relatable only
reasoning.because: Nobody knows Draftpace yet, so films show how it helps with real moments. Who it is not for, questions before buying, what you get and the price wait until there are users to sell to.

reasoning.decision: You own or rent a home and would rather be told what needs you this week than keep a mental list you know is incomplete. / You want the boring, expensive things caught early: the water heater, the gutters, the outside tap before the first freeze.
reasoning.because: The listing's own audience lines; the director writes for them.

reasoning.decision: In their words: The moment typed the way a person searches it, then what to do about it, then the product doing it.
reasoning.because: Best fit for a awareness film on Facebook feed video (platform fit 2, goal fit 3, already used for this product ×1). Other candidates: The moment (-3.0), Inside the tool (-7.4).
A situation people search for, "Homeownership feels like a full-time job", with the steps from "How to make a home binder you can safely share", and how Home Base helps.

reasoning.decision: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "tag"
reasoning.because: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "tag": things in the home are tagged, so scenes rise like a tag being lifted.
Camera "float": a gentle float that keeps a held frame alive without demanding attention.
Grounds light → light → ink → accent: a cool accent, so a darker ground is used for contrast at a turn.
Most of this audience never unmutes, so nothing depends on sound; cues are kept quieter and sparser for those who do.
Each scene is held for the time its words take to read on Facebook feed video (0.32s a word), inside 10–30s.
